title: Duchy of the Archipelago
capsule: The Duchy of the Archipelago (Ducato dell'Arcipelago) was a Latin feudal state carved from the Cyclades after the Fourth Crusade, founded in 1207 when the Venetian nobleman Marco I Sanudo, a kinsman of Doge Enrico Dandolo, seized Naxos with galleys from the Venetian Arsenal and took the title Duke of Naxos. Rather than holding the islands for Venice, Sanudo recognized the Latin Empire of Constantinople, parcelling Naxos into fiefs while distributing other Aegean islands to companions such as the Ghisi. Under his successors Angelo (r. 1227–1262) and Marco II (r. 1262–1303) the duchy was battered by the Byzantine reconquest led by the admiral Licario, which stripped away many islands and confined Sanudo rule largely to Naxos and Paros; Duke William I (r. 1303–1323) regained ground as the Byzantines withdrew their gains, only to face Catalan Company raids in the early fourteenth century.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The political succession of dukes is documented through Venetian archives and Byzantine chronicles; island-level territorial boundaries within the duchy are less precisely mapped, and some outer islands changed hands frequently between the duchy, Venice, and the Byzantines.
